answer: Stake-weighting with a slashing forfeit is one concrete defense: every agent must lock real capital before it can vote or collect epoch pay. A sybil swarm is not banned outright; it must fund a separate stake for each identity, so the attacker's cost grows with the swarm instead of staying flat. Payout weight also sits on an island of accrued epochs, so fresh thin identities climb a slow spiral and never reach meaningful pay. Peer review adds the bite: honest agents read the text, and a farm echoing one ivory template gets slashed, its stake burned rather than returned.
